Feature: Independent control register for each GPIO.
Test Description: Validate default reset values and masked read/write behavior for GPIO_8 to GPIO_27 control registers via register interface. Only readable fields are compared; only writable fields are updated. A known dynamic input bit is ignored during default comparison.
Meta Test Description:
The test performs two phases:
1) Default value check (chk_rst_val): For each address in addr_array, skip entries flagged in skip_rst_array or those with read_mask==0. Read the register, mask out bit0 (0xFFFFFFFE) to ignore a dynamic DIN-related bit, and compare against the corresponding expected default in default_value_array. Increment def_fail_cnt on mismatch.
2) Write/read check (chk_rd_wr): For each of six data patterns {0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000}, iterate all addresses. For each address not skipped and with nonzero write_mask, write (pattern & write_mask). Then, for each such address that is both writable and readable (read_mask!=0), read back (read_reg(addr) & read_mask). Compute wr_n = (~write_mask), then the expected value exp_val = ((pattern & read_mask & write_mask) | (wr_n & read_mask & default_value)). Compare data_rd with exp_val and increment wr_fail_cnt on mismatch. Test ends with finish(0) if both def_fail_cnt and wr_fail_cnt are zero; otherwise finish(1). A soft-reset routine exists but is compiled out (#ifdef 0).
Remarks: During default-value verification, ignore the DIN-related bit (bit0) by masking it to 0; only readable fields are compared and only writable fields are programmed; ensure the address list size matches the loop bound to avoid overruns; skips are honored for both default and read/write phases.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Verify default values for GPIO_8–GPIO_27: For each register, if default-check is enabled and the field is readable, read the register, ignore bit0, and compare with its documented default value. 2) Verify masked write/read behavior: For each test pattern, write the pattern to each register using its writable bits only, then read back and compare using read masks while preserving read-only bits at their default values. 3) Report pass if no mismatches are found in either phase; otherwise report fail with the first offending address and values.

title: GPIO Register Read/Write and Reset Default Validation
objective: Ensure GPIO_8–GPIO_27 registers hold correct reset defaults and honor read/write masks across representative data patterns.
steps: Initialize the test and counters for default and write/read failures.
For each GPIO register (GPIO_8–GPIO_27): if default-check is enabled and the field is readable, read the register, ignore bit0, and compare against its documented default.
For each data pattern, write to each GPIO register using only writable bits; then read back using read masks and evaluate expected values preserving read-only defaults.
Aggregate results and declare PASS if no mismatches occurred; otherwise declare FAIL with offending address and values.
expected_result: All default checks (with bit0 ignored) match expected defaults and all masked write/read checks match expected values for every pattern.

Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input
Test Description: Validate per-pin negative-edge interrupt generation for GPIO group by configuring each GPIO control register, enabling per-pin interrupts, generating a falling edge on each pin, and verifying masked interrupt status, proper clearing via raw interrupt clear, and system-level interrupt handling through the interrupt controller.
Meta Test Description:
The test configures the system interrupt controller and GPIO block, then iterates across 32 GPIO pins to verify negative-edge interrupt behavior:
- System IRQ enable: Depending on build flag (GPIO0 or GPIO1), enable the corresponding system interrupt source via intr_en1 and enable the GIC IRQ line (87 for GPIO0 or 88 for GPIO1).
- Precondition: Drive external stimulus register at 0xA0243FFC with 0xFFFFFFFF to set all inputs high.
- GPIO configuration loop (i = 0..31): For each pin, compute per-GPIO control address as (gpio_8 base + i*4) and write ((1<<20) | (1<<18) | (1<<16)) to configure interrupt type/polarity/enable fields for negative-edge detection, with brief wait.
- Per-pin test loop (i = 0..31):
  - Prepare wr_val = (1u << i).
  - Clear any stale raw interrupt by writing wr_val to gpio_intr_raw_stclr1.
  - Enable the pin's masked interrupt by writing wr_val to intr1_intr_en1; brief wait.
  - Set int_pend = 1 and generate a falling edge on the specific pin: write 0xFFFFFFFF to 0xA0243FFC, wait, then write bitwise NOT of wr_val to 0xA0243FFC causing only the target pin to go low.
  - Poll until the ISR clears int_pend or a timeout (5000 iterations) expires. On timeout, record an error ("Timeout waiting for GPIO%u negedge interrupt").
- ISR (Default_IRQHandler):
  - On entry, set int_pend = 0 and write 0xFFFFFFFF to 0xA0243FFC to drive all inputs high again.
  - Read the per-GPIO control register at (gpio_8 base + i*4) into rdata.
  - If (rdata & 0x1) != 0, record error (expected input state/flag is not asserted low after negedge).
  - If (rdata & 0x2) != 0, then:
    - Read masked group status intr1_intr_sts1; if (intr1_intr_sts1 & (1u<<i)) == 0, record error (expected masked status bit set).
    - Reprogram the per-GPIO control register with ((1<<20) | (1<<16)) to re-enable/retain configuration.
    - Clear the raw interrupt by writing (1u<<i) to gpio_intr_raw_stclr1.
    - Re-read intr1_intr_sts1; if not 0, record error (expected masked status cleared).
    - Clear system raw status via raw_stcr1 for the selected GPIO instance and clear the GIC IRQ (87/88 based on instance).
  - Else (if (rdata & 0x2) == 0), record error (expected edge event flag not observed).
- Test ends with finish(test_err).
Remarks: Ensure the system interrupt for the selected GPIO instance is enabled in the interrupt controller before testing. The input stimulus is generated via a memory-mapped register at 0xA0243FFC; platform must route this to GPIO inputs. Verify only one GPIO instance (GPIO0 or GPIO1) is selected per run so that the correct interrupt line is enabled and cleared.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable the system interrupt source for the target GPIO instance in intr_en1 and enable the corresponding GIC IRQ line. 2) Drive all GPIO inputs high using the stimulus register at 0xA0243FFC. 3) Configure each per-GPIO control register (gpio_8 to gpio_39) for negative-edge interrupt detection and enable the interrupt. 4) For each pin, clear any pending raw interrupt, enable its masked interrupt in intr1_intr_en1, and generate a falling edge only on that pin using 0xA0243FFC. 5) Wait for the ISR to trigger and service the interrupt; fail if the interrupt does not arrive within the timeout. 6) In ISR, verify the per-pin masked status in intr1_intr_sts1 is set, the input/flag state reflects the falling edge, then clear via gpio_intr_raw_stclr1 and confirm masked status clears; finally, clear the system-level raw status in raw_stcr1 and acknowledge the GIC. 7) Repeat for all pins and report pass if no mismatches or timeouts occur.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure: Initialization: test_err=0. If GPIO0: GIC_EnableIRQ(87); write_reg(intr_en1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR). If GPIO1: GIC_EnableIRQ(88); write_reg(intr_en1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR). write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0xFFFFFFFF). Config loop for i=0..31: addr1 = (gpio_8 + i*4); write_reg(addr1, (1u<<20)|(1u<<18)|(1u<<16)); wait_on(10). For each i=0..31: wr_val=(1u<<i); write_reg(gpio_intr_raw_stclr1, wr_val); write_reg(intr1_intr_en1, wr_val); wait_on(10); int_pend=1; write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0xFFFFFFFF); wait_on(30); write_reg(0xA0243FFC, ~wr_val); timeout=5000; while(int_pend && timeout--) wait_on(10); if(timeout==0){ printf("ERROR: Timeout waiting for GPIO%u negedge interrupt", i+8); test_err++; }. ISR Default_IRQHandler(): local_wr=(1u<<i); int_pend=0; write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0xFFFFFFFF); raddr=(gpio_8 + i*4); rdata=read_reg(raddr); if((rdata&0x1)!=0){ test_err++; } if((rdata&0x2)!=0){ rdata_grp=read_reg(intr1_intr_sts1); if((rdata_grp & local_wr)==0){ test_err++; } raddr2=(gpio_8 + i*4); write_reg(raddr2, (1u<<20)|(1u<<16)); write_reg(gpio_intr_raw_stclr1, local_wr); rdata_grp=read_reg(intr1_intr_sts1); if(rdata_grp!=0){ test_err++; } if GPIO0: write_reg(raw_stcr1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR); GIC_ClearIRQ(87); if GPIO1: write_reg(raw_stcr1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR); GIC_ClearIRQ(88); } else { test_err++; }. finalize: finish(test_err).

Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input.
Test Description: Validate positive-edge interrupt generation when enabling interrupts on all GPIO pads. The test configures each per-GPIO control register for positive-edge detection, sets GPIOs to input mode, enables the group interrupt, generates a rising edge on inputs, and verifies the group masked status asserts and clears. It also clears the system-level pending status and re-enables interrupts for subsequent iterations.
Meta Test Description:
test_case():
- If GPIO0 build: GIC_EnableIRQ(87). If GPIO1 build: GIC_EnableIRQ(88).
- test_err = 0.
- If GPIO0: write_reg(intr_en1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR). If GPIO1: write_reg(intr_en1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR).
- For i = 0..31: write_reg(gp0_gpio_8 + (i*4), 0x00020000) to enable positive-edge interrupt per pin (bit17=1).
- wait_on(10).
- Configure input mode across pads: write_reg(gpio_io_ctrl_group1, 0x000000FF); write_reg(gpio_io_ctrl_group2, 0x000000FF); write_reg(gpio_io_ctrl_group3, 0x000000FF); write_reg(gpio_io_ctrl_group4, 0x000000FF).
- wait_on(10).
- Enable masked interrupts for the group: write_reg(gp0_intr2_intr_en1, 0xFFFFFFFF).
- For i = 0..31 loop:
  - Drive external stimulus low then high to produce a single rising edge: write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0x00000000); wait_on(10); set int_pend = 1; write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0xFFFFFFFF).
  - Timeout wait: timeout = 2000; while (int_pend == 1 && --timeout > 0) wait_on(10).
  - If timeout == 0: printf("ERROR: Timeout waiting for GPIO IRQ at i=%u", i); test_err++; break.
  - Optionally drive low again for next iteration: write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0x00000000); wait_on(10).
- finish(test_err).

Default_IRQHandler():
- wr_val = (1 << i); int_pend = 0.
- rdata_grp = read_reg(gp0_intr1_intr_sts1); mask group during service: write_reg(gp0_intr2_intr_en1, 0x00000000).
- If (rdata_grp & 0xFFFFFFFF) != 0: success log (if enabled) else: print error and increment test_err.
- Clear per-pin raw status for all 32 pins: for j = 0..31: write_reg(gp0_gpio_8 + (j*4), 0x00010000). wait_on(2).
- Read group status again: rdata_grp = read_reg(gp0_intr1_intr_sts1). If rdata_grp == 0x0: success; else: print error and test_err++.
- If GPIO0: write_reg(raw_stcr1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR); rdata = read_reg(raw_stcr1); if (rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR) != 0 then error++.
- If GPIO1: write_reg(raw_stcr1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR); rdata = read_reg(raw_stcr1); if (rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR) != 0 then error++.
- Re-enable group masked interrupts: write_reg(gp0_intr2_intr_en1, 0xFFFFFFFF).
- If GPIO0: GIC_ClearIRQ(87); If GPIO1: GIC_ClearIRQ(88).
Remarks: Ensure the corresponding GPIO instance interrupt is enabled in the system interrupt controller before testing and that the external stimulus at 0xA0243FFC is routed to GPIO inputs. Mask the group interrupt during ISR service to avoid re-entrancy, clear all per-pin raw statuses, verify the group status returns to zero, and clear the system-level raw status before re-enabling interrupts.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable the GPIO instance interrupt in the system interrupt controller (intr_en1) and enable the corresponding GIC IRQ line (87 or 88). 2) Configure each per-GPIO control register for positive-edge detection across 32 pins. 3) Set all GPIO pads to input mode using the IO control group registers. 4) Enable the masked group interrupt output. 5) Generate a rising edge on the GPIO inputs and wait for the ISR to run within the timeout. 6) In the ISR, verify that the group masked interrupt status is set, mask the group, clear all per-pin raw statuses, confirm the group status clears, clear the system raw status (raw_stcr1), and then re-enable group interrupts and acknowledge the GIC. 7) Repeat the edge generation and verification loop for the configured iterations and report overall pass/fail.
